tool.name: Cyclospora HDS sheet
tool.description: collect per-specimen Cyclospora haplotype calls into one CDC wide sheet
tool.command:
## The image runs with contain / cleanenv / no-mount tmp, so /tmp is read-only on ## a compute node and TMPDIR is empty. Give it a home inside the job directory. mkdir -p wrk calls && export TMPDIR="\$(pwd)/wrk" &&
## Galaxy stores every dataset as dataset_<n>.dat, which destroys the specimen id ## for any caller TSV that does not carry one in a column. Stage the collection ## into calls/ under its element identifier so the builder's filename fallback can ## still recover the specimen. Non-portable characters are folded to '_'; a ## collision therefore makes `ln -s` fail loudly rather than silently drop a file. #import re #for $c in $calls ln -s '$c' 'calls/${re.sub("[^A-Za-z0-9_.-]", "_", str($c.element_identifier))}.tsv' && #end for
python '$__tool_directory__/build_hds_sheet.py' --calls calls --out '$sheet' #if $specimens --specimens '$specimens' #end if $drop_novel #if $emit_summary --summary '$summary' #end if

param.name: calls
param.label: Per-specimen haplotype call TSVs
param.help: A 'list' collection of caller output: the long TSV from Cyclospora PART haplotypes, the TSV from Cyclospora Mt-Junction, or both for the same specimens. The file TYPE is detected from its header, never from its name. The specimen id comes from the file's own 'specimen' column when there is one, and otherwise from the element identifier - so name elements after the specimen, and run the junction caller with its 'Emit specimen column' option on.

param.name: specimens
param.label: Specimen list (optional)
param.help: One specimen id per line. Fixes the row order and, crucially, FORCES a row for a specimen that produced no calls at all - which is how a whole-specimen failure enters the sheet as an all-empty row rather than vanishing. Without it, rows are the specimens actually seen, sorted. Ids present in the collection but absent from this list are dropped with a warning on stderr.

param.name: drop_novel
param.label: Keep only named reference haplotypes
param.help: Discard haplotypes that did not match a named reference (the '<PART>_NOV_<md5>' and junction NOVEL columns). Off by default: novel haplotypes carry real discriminating signal, and the pre-registered analysis keeps them. Turning this on reproduces the 'knownonly' sheets.

param.name: emit_summary
param.label: Also emit the per-specimen audit table
param.help: Per specimen: how many haplotypes, how many locus blocks were called, and which came out empty. The sheet format cannot distinguish 'amplicon dropped out' from 'locus was called but no haplotype cleared the gates' - both are an empty block. This table is what makes that auditable.

tool.help:
**Cyclospora HDS sheet** — stage 6 of the *Cyclospora cayetanensis* LoFreq/PyEuk typing arm. It collects the per-specimen call TSVs written by *Cyclospora PART haplotypes* and *Cyclospora Mt-Junction* into the single wide haplotype data sheet (HDS) that PyEuk consumes.
-----
## The sheet format has three states, and the third is the subtle one
``` Seq_ID Hap_1 Hap_2 Hap_3 ... SPEC_A X X SPEC_B X ```
| cell | meaning | |---|---| | `X` | haplotype **present** in that specimen | | empty | haplotype **absent**, at a locus that **was** called | | **every column of one locus empty** | that locus was **NOT CALLED** — amplicon dropout |
There is no separate missing-data code. The entirely empty locus block *is* the code, and PyEuk's dropout handling keys off it. This is why the upstream callers must emit no rows at all for a locus that failed its coverage gate, and why this tool never writes a placeholder into an empty block.
The format has one irreducible ambiguity, inherited from CDC: a locus that *was* sequenced deeply enough to call, but whose candidate haplotypes all failed the frequency/read gates, also produces an empty block and is indistinguishable from dropout. Turn on **the per-specimen audit table** to see how many blocks came out empty for each specimen; the PART caller's own summary output resolves which of the two it was, because it reports the actual spanning depth.
-----
## Inputs
- **Per-specimen haplotype call TSVs** — a `list` collection. Elements may be PART-caller output, junction-caller output, or both; mixing them in one collection is the normal case. Each file's type is decided by its header line, not its name, and a file that is neither is skipped with a warning.
- **Specimen list** *(optional)* — one id per line. Two effects, both worth having in a production run: it fixes the row order, and it forces a row for a specimen that produced no calls whatsoever, so a specimen that failed outright is visible in the sheet as an all-empty row instead of silently disappearing.
- **Keep only named reference haplotypes** *(optional)* — drops `<PART>_NOV_<md5>` and novel junction columns. Off by default.
## Outputs
- **CDC HDS sheet** (tabular) — `Seq_ID` then one column per haplotype, columns sorted, `X` for present. - **Locus block audit** (tabular, optional) — `specimen`, `n_haplotypes`, `n_loci_called`, `n_loci_empty`, `empty_loci`.
-----
## Where the specimen id comes from
Galaxy names every dataset `dataset_<n>.dat`, so a filename is not a specimen id here. In order of preference:
1. the file's own `specimen` column — PART-caller output always has one, and the junction caller writes one when run with **Emit specimen column** on. **Use this.** The column wins over everything else. 2. otherwise, the **element identifier** of the collection element, which this tool stages onto disk as `<identifier>.tsv` before reading.
So: name collection elements after the specimen, and switch the junction caller's specimen column on. A file that mixes two specimen ids in its `specimen` column is rejected rather than merged.
-----
## No reference data is needed here, on purpose
`markers.fa`, `parts.bed`, `haplotypes78.fa` and `junction.fa` are **not** inputs to this tool and are not bundled with it. Haplotype naming — the only step that consults a reference — happens upstream in the callers, which is where those files belong. By the time calls reach this tool, every haplotype already carries its final name, and the sheet is pure aggregation over those names. Giving this step a reference input would create a way for the sheet to disagree with the calls it was built from, for no gain.
The only file bundled with the wrapper is `build_hds_sheet.py` itself, via `required_files`.
-----
Ported from `pyeuk-bench/lofreq_arm/build_sheets.py`, extended to read per-specimen files and to carry the Mt-Junction locus. Reproduces the reference sheets byte for byte; see `tools/cyclospora/VALIDATION.md`.
